open_points.subject: secret-bearing service file
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone, the owner included, and never used as an output” conflicts with “the kernel does not inspect file content” and with M22 allowing “the owner inspecting its bytes … whatever the class”; the removed text no longer says how a secret inside a file the kernel only moves is treated.
open_points.question: When a service returns a file whose bytes contain a configured secret verbatim, is that file a secret-echoing answer body that must be withheld and excluded from outputs, or an opaque file governed only by its disclosure class; specifically, may it be inspected by the owner, moved to another service, or supplied to a function node?
options: Treat the file as opaque and protect it only by its disclosure class, allowing the otherwise-authorized reads and node deliveries
Treat it as a secret-echoing body and withhold it from every reader and downstream node
Apply secret withholding to non-file answer bodies only and state that scope explicitly
open_points.default_guess: Treat files as opaque and protect them only by their disclosure class, because K-10 says the kernel does not inspect file content.
